- P001b (memo 001) pushes +1 — Office-buying and transfers for cash become prosecutable; commanders relieved for cause with evidence an adviser could never produce
- P001b (memo 001) depends — Relief for cause needs replacements; without a pool of honest officers, removal leaves vacancies
- P002b (memo 002) pushes +1 — Selection for a province or district becomes a reward for merit in the field, and the examination creates a record of officers' ability that promotion boards can use
- P002a (memo 002) depends — Military Security Service and ARVN intelligence must accept Special Branch primacy on the VCI
- P002b (memo 002) depends — The candidate pool is the officer corps and a thin civil service; merit selection cannot select merit that does not exist
- P004a (memo 004) depends — A better rifle does not make a unit go out at night or accept contact; leaders decide that
- P004b (memo 004) depends — Marksmen must be selected on skill, not on favour, and employed by squad leaders who understand them
- P006c (memo 006) depends — Advice changes a commander who will listen; it does not replace one who will not

### ARVN.self_sufficiency
- P004a (memo 004) depends — M855A1, optics, batteries and URG-I parts all come from the United States; the RVNAF cannot make or repair them at depth, so the rearmament deepens the supply dependence that 1973–75 punished
- P005c (memo 005) pushes -1 — Defence of besieged positions is built around an American bomber and American coordinates the RVNAF can never own
- P006c (memo 006) pushes -1 — An adviser qualified and trusted to call American air and artillery becomes the advised unit's means of fire; better advising of fire deepens the dependence the withdrawal punishes, unless the adviser is directed to train Vietnamese observers to replace him

### GVN.admin_capacity
- P001b (memo 001) pushes +1 — Budgets executed as voted; province and district funds reaching their purpose
- P001a (memo 001) depends — Province land services and village committees must exist and work
- P002b (memo 002) pushes +2 — Chiefs chosen for ability, kept long enough to learn a province, and inspected by a body they do not command: the single largest lever on provincial administration
- P002a (memo 002) depends — Courts, prosecutors and the province and district chief direct and protect the police
- P006a (memo 006) depends — The district chief runs the DIOCC; the magistrates decide the cases

### GVN.corruption
- P001b (memo 001) pushes -2 — Investigation, prosecution and an aid-suspension lever against ghost payrolls, sale of offices and diversion; substantial, not transformative, because the enforcer's reach stops where the junta's protection begins
- P001a (memo 001) depends — Fees to accept applications, collusion with landlords and false worship-land claims hollow out the programme (P001b)
- P002b (memo 002) pushes -1 — A post that cannot be bought cannot be farmed to repay the price; vetting and asset declarations close the front door, while the side doors of contracts, rice and the draft stay open
- P002a (memo 002) depends — Police posts are bought and sold, checkpoints become toll gates, and Special Branch files can be sold; the Commission Against Corruption (P001b) polices the police
- P002b (memo 002) depends — Examinations can be leaked and boards bought; the Commission Against Corruption (P001b) vets candidates and audits the Board
- P004a (memo 004) depends — Rifles, optics, batteries and ammunition are saleable; leakage to the market and to the Front is set by command honesty
- P006a (memo 006) depends — Bribes for release and false denunciations for feud undo the evidence standard
- P006c (memo 006) depends — An adviser who reports corruption needs a lever that acts on the report

### GVN.political_stability
- P001a (memo 001) pushes -1 — Expropriates the landed class from which much of the officer corps and the civil service come; a coup grievance in a junta already prone to coups
- P001b (memo 001) pushes -1 — Threatens the incomes of the generals who make and unmake governments; prosecutions become coup grievances and coup weapons
- P001a (memo 001) depends — The decree must survive the next coup; each new junta may reopen it
- P001b (memo 001) depends — The commission lives only while some faction in Saigon protects it
- P002a (memo 002) pushes +1 — A Special Branch that watches the generals as well as the VC, and a police that is not one faction's instrument, slightly raises the cost of a coup; the reform is itself a prize for the faction that captures it
- P002b (memo 002) pushes -1 — Takes from the generals their most valuable patronage; a coup grievance in 1964, and a coup-maker's first target is the selection board
- P002a (memo 002) depends — Every junta since 1955 has used the police as a political instrument; the Director General's fixed term survives only while a coup does not sweep it away
- P002b (memo 002) depends — The Board and the two-year tenure survive only as long as the government that decreed them, and the next coup may sweep both
- P006a (memo 006) depends — Each coup changes the committee's chairman and tempts its use against the opposition
- P006c (memo 006) depends — Counterparts appointed and removed by coup outlast no adviser

### INTEL.penetration
- P001b (memo 001) pushes -1 — Investigations of officials who sell documents, passes and posts uncover some of the enemy's purchased agents
- P001b (memo 001) depends — A commission holding the regime's secrets is a target for the enemy's agents as well as the generals'
- P002a (memo 002) pushes -1 — Special Branch counter-intelligence and vetting against an enemy that has had agents in the police and the RVNAF for a decade; partial, and itself a target
- P002a (memo 002) depends — A Special Branch penetrated by the enemy hands him its informants
- P003a (memo 003) depends — Anything shared with the Joint General Staff can reach the enemy; the product is only as secret as the least secure office that reads it
- P005a (memo 005) depends — B-52 strikes in the South need GVN clearance; a penetrated clearance chain warns the target whatever the bomb
- P006a (memo 006) depends — A fused file in a penetrated centre is the enemy's list of our informants

### POP.civilian_harm
- P001a (memo 001) pushes +1 — Titled families and land committee members in contested hamlets become targets of the enemy's security sections (F001-8)
- P002a (memo 002) pushes -1 — Arrest on evidence and detention under review replace part of the military's sweep-and-detain; offset in part by enemy terror against resident constables
- P003b (memo 003) pushes +1 — Night movement tracks in the Delta and the coastal plain are fired on under the historical rules; a radar cannot tell a farmer's sampan from a VC supply sampan
- P005b (memo 005) pushes -1 — Point targets no longer need area boxes; offset by more targets struck
- P005c (memo 005) pushes -1 — Smaller bombs on single aimpoints instead of a carpet of 108
- P006a (memo 006) pushes -1 — Warrants, capture-first rules and no quotas against the historical Phoenix of feud and quota; the PRUs remain the risk

### RFPF.effectiveness
- P001a (memo 001) pushes +1 — A Popular Forces militiaman who owns the field he guards has a reason to fight at night that pay alone does not give
- P001a (memo 001) depends — Territorial forces hold titled hamlets after the land teams leave
- P002b (memo 002) pushes +1 — The province and district chief commands the Regional and Popular Forces; a competent chief who stays two years is the largest single improvement territorial forces can receive without new equipment
- P002a (memo 002) depends — Popular Forces hold the village with the constable at night; the police post is not a fort
- P004a (memo 004) pushes +1 — The outpost platoon holds its wall against a VC local-force company with 30-round magazines and a red dot instead of carbines and Garands; the territorial forces are rearmed five years before 1969
- P004a (memo 004) depends — The rifle's value in the hamlet depends on whether the platoon is present and awake after dark
- P006c (memo 006) pushes +1 — Subsector advisers and mobile teams who know the posts and the district chief

### US.casualties
- P004a (memo 004) pushes -1 — Fewer men lost in the first seconds of the meeting engagement; the rifle that does not jam in the Hill 881 sense
- P004a (memo 004) depends — The fraction of US deaths taken from small arms in the first seconds of contact, against the much larger fraction from mines, booby traps, mortars and RPGs that no rifle touches
- P005c (memo 005) pushes -1 — Closer, faster heavy fire in defence of besieged positions
- P006b (memo 006) pushes -1 — Collective training and stable leaders cut the losses of the new man; the unit's first month in a new area offsets part of it
- P006b (memo 006) depends — Losses within a tour are refilled by individuals; heavy losses return the unit to individual replacement in practice

### US.personnel_demand
- P002a (memo 002) pushes +1 — About 520 Americans, of whom about 150 in uniform, mostly in the provinces
- P003a (memo 003) pushes +1 — About 220 spaces of scarce specialists: U-2 pilots, sensor technicians, imagery analysts and Vietnamese-language SIGINT linguists
- P003b (memo 003) pushes +1 — About 380 spaces: pilots and sensor operators for a 24-hour orbit, maintainers, contractor engineers and an exploitation cell
- P006a (memo 006) pushes +1 — About 600 Americans in the centres and the exploitation cell
- P006b (memo 006) pushes +1 — Overlap at each relief in place and a larger rotation base of formed units without the reserves
- P006b (memo 006) depends — The size of the force in theater sets the size of the rotation base
- P006c (memo 006) depends — The selected pool is the same pool of good captains and NCOs that American units need

### US.political_tolerance
- P001b (memo 001) pushes +1 — Visible reform and true strength returns modestly lengthen tolerance, with negative spikes from corruption headlines (F001-14)
- P001a (memo 001) depends — Congress funds the compensation bonds over eight years
- P001b (memo 001) depends — Washington must accept slower military operations while commands are purged
- P002a (memo 002) depends — Congress funds a police programme that its critics will call a secret police
- P002b (memo 002) depends — Washington must accept that a chief who will not falsify returns reports bad news
- P003a (memo 003) depends — A lost U-2 is a public event; the 1960 and 1962 losses are in every politician's memory
- P004a (memo 004) pushes +1 — Small: no 1967 rifle scandal, no Ichord subcommittee hearings, no letters home about a rifle that jams; fewer dead in the first seconds of contact
- P005a (memo 005) depends — Every expansion of B-52 targeting is a Washington decision
- P006a (memo 006) depends — A programme described as assassination can be ended by Congress
- P006b (memo 006) depends — No reserve mobilization; the rotation base comes from the active forces and the draft

### US.unit_quality
- P004a (memo 004) pushes +1 — No 1967 M16 jamming crisis, a red-dot sight in every rifleman's hands, and M855A1 through brush and light cover
- P006b (memo 006) pushes +2 — Squads, platoons and commanders who trained together and stay together for the tour; no six-month command
- P006c (memo 006) pushes -1 — The selected captains, majors and senior NCOs are taken from the American units

## Settled positions on these variables

- **POSTNA-1** · vars: GVN.political_stability, POP.gvn_legitimacy, POP.land_tenure · The binding deficit on the opening date is political: no provision that leaves the Saigon government's standing in the countryside unchanged moves the end state above rung (b), whatever it does to the enemy's forces (TNA G-1)
- **POSTNA-2** · vars: POP.night_control, RFPF.effectiveness · Night control of a hamlet is held only by security resident in it with a means of calling help and a reaction that arrives in the dark; mobile forces that leave at dusk do not change it (TNA G-2)
- **POSTNA-5** · vars: US.political_tolerance, US.credibility_gap, US.casualties · The American political clock is spent by casualties, cost and time, and fastest by the discovery that reported progress was false; a provision that improves a metric without improving the war shortens the clock (TNA G-5, G-10)
- **POSTNA-6** · vars: ADVISE.leverage, POP.gvn_legitimacy · Advisory leverage trades short-run effectiveness against long-run legitimacy; no position on that line is free, and every proposal to increase leverage states what it costs the Republic's claim to be its own government (TNA G-6)
- **POS001-2** · vars: GVN.corruption, ADVISE.leverage, GVN.political_stability · An independent anti-corruption body in the Republic survives only with a Vietnamese patron and an American lever; its durable effect is on muster, pay and documentary cases below the top, and its reach upward ends when the lever lapses with the American drawdown (001 §4.P4)
- **POS002-2** · vars: GVN.admin_capacity, ADVISE.leverage, GVN.political_stability · Merit selection of province and district chiefs survives the coups only with the American aid lever behind it; when the lever lapses with the drawdown the President captures the Board without abolishing it, and its durable gain is the chiefs' experience below the palace (002 §4.P4, EV002-6)
- **POS002-3** · vars: GVN.police, GVN.political_stability, POP.gvn_legitimacy · A stronger and better-recorded police in a coup-prone state is used by the government of the day against its domestic opposition, and its records are a list of loyalties the enemy can capture; both costs are paid and do not outweigh the gain in the held belt (002 F002-9, F002-16; §4.P2, §4.P3)
- **POS003-3** · vars: US.political_tolerance, US.credibility_gap · In this war no attack of 4 August 1964 was claimed and Pierce Arrow was not flown; the Southeast Asia Resolution rests on the attack of 2 August, and the Tonkin deception is not part of the credibility gap in any later phase (003 §4.P1, §4.P3; EV000-3)
- **POS004-1** · vars: RFPF.effectiveness, POP.night_control, ENEMY.engagement_control · Infantry small arms change how the fights the enemy accepts go, never which fights he accepts; at the outpost their value equals the platoon's presence after dark and the reaction behind it, and the enemy's answer to a better-armed post is to attack what is not rearmed (004 F004-1, F004-3, F004-16; §4.P1)
- **POS004-2** · vars: ARVN.effectiveness, US.unit_quality, US.political_tolerance · In this war the ARVN and the RF/PF carry modern carbines from 1964, and the 1967 M16 crisis and inquiry and the 1968–69 rearmament do not occur; from 1969 the historical army has caught up, and the remaining difference is the squad gun, the marksman and the practice (004 F004-6; §4.P2–P4)
- **POS004-3** · vars: ARVN.self_sufficiency, LOG.distribution · Abundant American ammunition from 1964 deepens the RVNAF's dependence on volume of fire; the 1974 ration falls hardest on the squad gun, and the divisional hoards built against it are lost in the collapse of March 1975 (004 F004-15; §4.P6)
- **POS005-2** · vars: ARVN.self_sufficiency, FIX.capability, US.political_tolerance · In this war the defence of besieged positions from 1965 rests on the B-52J and an American coordinate cell; it is far stronger while American air power is present and leaves the RVNAF more dependent on it when it goes (005 §2 F005-20)
- **POSCP01-1** · vars: US.political_tolerance, US.credibility_gap · The small gains on the American clock in memoranda 001–005 (no Tonkin deception, honest damage assessment, no M16 scandal, a conviction in 1967, fewer prisoners and no Bach Mai in 1972) narrow the credibility gap and do not move tolerance by a band in any phase, because the clock was spent by the casualties of 1965–68 and by Tet, which no provision changed and one made sharper (CP01 §3; C003-3)
- **POSCP01-2** · vars: ADVISE.leverage, ARVN.self_sufficiency · In this war the American lever was used to protect the Republic's honest institutions from its own governments and never to make the Republic own the instruments of the conventional war (coordinates, reconnaissance, guided weapons, ammunition stocks); the dependence deepened by memoranda 004 and 005 was never contested by the instrument that could have contested it (CP01 §3)
- **POSCP01-3** · vars: ARVN.leadership, GVN.admin_capacity · The Commission, the Selection Board and every provision that needs a competent leader draw on one pool of perhaps 900–1,200 honest, able field-grade officers in 1964–66; the pool is spent several times over and the divisions are the loser each time, which is why G-4 stays open while the provinces improve (CP01 §3)
- **POS006-2** · vars: US.unit_quality, US.casualties, ENEMY.engagement_control · Unit rotation makes the American battalion fight better in the contacts it gets and changes neither which contacts it gets nor the late-war breakdown of discipline; it gives the enemy a relief window to aim at, and it does not prevent atrocity (006 F006-6, F006-16, F006-19)
- **POS006-3** · vars: ADVISE.leverage, ARVN.self_sufficiency · The selected advisory corps deepens influence, not authority; its durable values are continuity across the American unit's relief and honest reporting, and a better adviser deepens the advised unit's dependence on American fire unless he hands over the radio, which works for artillery, the VNAF and medevac and not for the B-52J (006 F006-2, F006-17, F006-23)
- **POS006-4** · vars: FIND.vci, INTEL.penetration, GVN.political_stability · In this war the national Phung Hoang file, built to warrant standard from 1964, was moved into the Central Intelligence Organization in 1970, consolidated in one building for the 1971 election, and captured intact on 30 April 1975 with the I Corps files a month earlier; the accuracy that made it valuable to the Republic made it more valuable to the victors (006 §4.P4, §4.P6; EV002-6, EV000-94, EV000-98)
- **POS006-6** · vars: US.unit_quality, US.casualties, US.personnel_demand · In this war American battalions deploy, are relieved and withdraw as units; the estimated saving of 1,000–2,000 American lives in 1966–69 is a judgment on a rate of 3–6 percent shown so far only at Dien Ban, and does not move the casualty band (006 §4.P2, §4.H; EV006-3)

## Provision index (every provision in theater)

- **P001a** · Land-to-the-Tiller Programme, 1964 (accelerated and enhanced): zero retention of tenanted rice land, free distribution to the present tiller, confirmation of Viet Minh and Viet Cong distributions, US-financed landlord compensation, and a fit-for-purpose aerial-photo titling apparatus · One national programme: about 1.0–1.2 million ha of tenanted land to about 850,000–950,000 families [E: Prosterman's 1960–61 tenancy census and the GAO's 1970 LTTT target of 1 million ha to 800,000 tenants] · spaces ~260 US personnel, of whom ~60 military spaces [E: USAID land and survey advisers in each province plus an Army engineer topographic detachment; the 1970s LTTT advisory staff was 31] · SECURE, SUBVERT · arrives 1964-01-01 · active · memo 001
- **P001b** · GVN Anti-Corruption Programme with Enforcement Mechanism: an independent Commission Against Corruption on the Hong Kong ICAC model with powers of arrest, search, seizure and compelled asset declaration, a special anti-corruption court, an independent RVNAF pay-and-muster verification service, and a joint US–GVN Aid Compliance Board empowered to suspend aid to a command or ministry · One national commission of about 2,000 Vietnamese staff with about 320 US advisers, investigators and auditors [E: ICAC's 1,213 staff for a city of about 7 million, scaled for a country of about 15 million and an armed force of about 514,000] · spaces ~320 US personnel, of whom ~140 military spaces [E: Army CID agents, finance and audit officers and muster teams; the rest USAID, Treasury and GAO-trained civilians] · ADVISE, SUSTAIN, SECURE · arrives 1964-01-01 · active · memo 001
- **P002a** · National Police Reform Programme, 1964: a resident rural constabulary with a police post in every village, a rebuilt Police Special Branch with sole charge of intelligence on the VC infrastructure, a Police Field Force raised two years early, a national identity and family census, a police pay and career statute, and judicial safeguards on arrest and detention · One national programme: the National Police grown from about 19,000–22,000 in January 1964 to about 70,000 by the end of 1966 and about 95,000 by the end of 1968, of whom about 24,000 rural police resident in villages and about 7,500 Special Branch [E: village and district counts of the period, the historical growth to 88,000 by 1970, and training throughput] · spaces ~520 US personnel, of whom ~150 military spaces [E: about 300 USAID Public Safety advisers against the historical 144 of December 1965, about 150 Army military police and CID training-team spaces, about 70 contractor technicians for the identity system]; about 40 British, Malaysian and Australian police advisers outside US spaces · SECURE, FIND, SUBVERT · arrives 1964-01-01 · active · memo 002
- **P002b** · Provincial Administration Reform, 1964: merit-based selection of province and district chiefs by an independent Provincial Administration Selection Board, by competitive examination, assessment and vetting, with appointment from a ranked list, a guaranteed two-year tenure removable only for cause, an independent Inspectorate of Provincial Administration, a pay and allowance reform, and a mandatory course before posting · About 290 chief posts (44–45 province chiefs and 239–243 district chiefs) and about 330 deputy posts, filled by competition over 1964–65 [E: the province and district counts of the period, one deputy for administration in each province and district] · spaces ~90 US personnel, of whom ~30 military spaces [E: a small advisory staff to the Selection Board and the Inspectorate, assessment-centre specialists, and province senior advisers' share of the inspection work] · SECURE, ADVISE · arrives 1964-01-01 · active · memo 002
- **P003a** · Lockheed Martin U-2S Dragon Lady (Block 20), 2026 configuration: ASARS-2A synthetic aperture radar with moving-target indication, SYERS-2C multispectral electro-optical and infrared camera, ASIP signals intelligence payload, with a deployable ground exploitation station · 2 aircraft [U] · spaces ~220 [E: four to five pilots and a mobile-crew cell, about 90 maintainers and life-support technicians, about 20 contractor field engineers, and an exploitation and SIGINT cell of about 100 in shifts] · FIND, STRIKE, INTERDICT · arrives 1964-01-01 · active · memo 003
- **P003b** · Northrop Grumman RQ-4B Global Hawk Block 40, 2026 configuration: MP-RTIP active electronically scanned array radar with simultaneous ground moving-target indication and synthetic aperture imaging, with a Launch and Recovery Element and a Mission Control Element · 4 aircraft [U] · spaces ~380 [E: six to seven three-person mission crews for one continuous orbit, an LRE detachment, about 140 maintainers and contractor technicians, and a GMTI and radar-imagery exploitation cell of about 150 in shifts] · FIND, INTERDICT, STRIKE · arrives 1964-01-01 · active · memo 003
- **P004a** · M4A1 carbine with the Upper Receiver Group – Improved (URG-I: Geissele Automatics upper, Daniel Defense 14.5-inch 1:7 barrel, mid-length gas, Mk16 13.5-inch M-LOK rail, SureFire SF4P flash hider) and Aimpoint CompM5 2 MOA red-dot sight, firing M855A1 5.56mm, 2026 configuration · All rifles and carbines of US forces and the RVNAF, and all RF/PF [U]: a first increment of about 600,000 carbines and sights in 1964, rising to about 1.7–1.9 million cumulative by 1972 [E: RVNAF 514,000 in 1964 and about 1,048,000 in 1971–72 per S9, US strength rising to about 540,000 at peak, plus a 10% float] · spaces ~250 [E: about 120 new-equipment training spaces in the first year, about 80 small-arms and optics repair technicians at the depots, and about 50 added small-arms advisers to the RF/PF training centres; no troop ceiling is set, but each space still costs] · SECURE, FIX, ADVISE, SUSTAIN · arrives 1964-01-01 · active · memo 004
- **P004b** · Knight's Armament Company M110A2 7.62mm semi-automatic rifle (20-inch free-floated match barrel, integral suppressor, 12-inch M-LOK handguard, collapsible stock) with SIG Sauer TANGO6T 1-6x24mm first-focal-plane illuminated variable-power scope, firing M118LR and M80A1 7.62mm, issued one per infantry squad as the designated marksman's rifle, 2026 configuration · One per US and ARVN infantry squad [U]: about 5,000 rifles and scopes in 1964, about 13,000 cumulative by 1972 [E: about 120 ARVN, Ranger, Airborne and Marine battalions of about 36 squads in 1964 rising to about 180 by 1972, plus up to about 112 US Army and Marine manoeuvre battalions at the 1968–69 peak, plus a 10% float] · spaces ~120 [E: marksman instructor teams of about 60 at the training centres and about 60 match-rifle and scope armourers; the marksmen themselves are squad members already counted] · FIX, SECURE, STRIKE · arrives 1964-01-01 · active · memo 004

## Gap register (latest status)

- **G-1** · A state without a foundation · narrowed · Land, police, merit chiefs and the Commission give the Republic a government in the held belt from 1964; it is captured by the palace when the American lever lapses in 1970–71, and its foundation in the countryside does not carry into the conventional war (CP01)
- **G-2** · Who holds the countryside after dark · narrowed · Posts with their platoon and a reaction hold about nine attacks in ten, and the held belt is held at night before Tet; outside it nothing has changed, and every programme stops at its edge (CP01)
- **G-3** · Identifying the infrastructure inside the population · narrowed · A Special Branch, a census and a land register identify the infrastructure in the held belt from 1964 and drive it out; it moves to the towns, penetrates the Branch, and turns the census into the Hue lists (CP01)
- **G-4** · The officer corps: selection, leadership, desertion, corruption · open · Musters, pay at the parade, merit chiefs and a conviction improve the provinces and the pay; the divisions' leadership is unchanged because the same few honest officers are spent on every reform at once (CP01)
- **G-5** · The American political clock · open · Small gains in the credibility gap from five memoranda; tolerance unmoved in every phase, because it was spent by the casualties of 1965–68 and by Tet (CP01)
- **G-6** · Advisory leverage and its limits · open · The Aid Compliance Board is a real lever until 1969 and lapses with the withdrawal; it was used for governance and never for the RVNAF's self-sufficiency (CP01)
- **G-7** · Finding and fixing the main force · open · The enemy is easier to see in the open and exactly as hard to find under canopy; he still chooses every fight except the siege (CP01)
- **G-8** · Sanctuary and the theory of attrition · open · Cambodia is counted from 1965 and its caches fall in ten days in 1970; the sanctuaries still regenerate the main force in every phase (CP01)
- **G-9** · The Trail: throughput required against capacity · open · Measured from 1965 instead of guessed; bombing taxes it by about a tenth at best, and the B-52J built it a net with no single point of failure (CP01)
- **G-10** · The measurement problem · narrowed · The radar's ledger, the musters and the Phoenix audit give honest counts of the Trail, the army and the infrastructure; body count and the Hamlet Evaluation System remain as corrupt as before (CP01)
- **G-11** · The sea and Sihanoukville · narrowed · The sea route closed in 1964; Sihanoukville opened eighteen months early and was counted, not stopped, until Lon Nol closed it in 1970 (CP01)
- **G-12** · Air power against a dispersed, night-moving enemy · narrowed · Decisive against the measured siege and the fixed crossing; nothing against a regiment under canopy or an attack on a post at night, and none of it Vietnamese (CP01)
- **G-13** · No single manager of the war · open · CORDS on its historical date and form; the provisions created no single manager, only better inheritances for it (CP01)
- **G-14** · No lever on Hanoi's will · open · Nothing in the force reaches the Politburo; reform raised its urgency without changing its decisions (CP01)
- **G-15** · The theater base · open · Unchanged by any provision; the rearmament's ammunition and the J's kits ride the historical base (CP01)
- **G-16** · Personnel spaces · open · About 2,400 spaces in the Republic across eleven provisions, trivial against a ceiling of none; no provision has yet changed how American soldiers are rotated or how advisers are chosen (CP01)
